Congenital generalized hair abnormalities define the dermatologic axis. Dental abnormalities and hearing impairment are each annotated in 80-99%, supporting gastrointestinal and otologic involvement.

Absorptive hypercalciuria is a calcium metabolic disorder. Increased urinary calcium does not itself establish kidney damage; nephrolithiasis is separately diagnosed and does not establish additional renal involvement here.
Appendiceal mucinous tumour origin supports gastrointestinal primary labeling. Peritoneal dissemination adds no separate axis, and respiratory insufficiency is occasional (5-29%).
Metabolic enzyme deficiency is primary. Cataracts affect 3/4 patients, and neurodevelopmental impairment is a core manifestation. Hepatic, cardiac and pancreatic injury each affect only 1/4.
Both hepatocytes and intrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis. The broader digestive-system parent does not justify an additional gastrointestinal label.

Developmental delay, trichomegaly and brachycephaly define the three primary axes. Structural oral abnormalities in 1/2 patients support gastrointestinal involvement; ribosomal dysfunction alone does not justify haematologic labeling.
